title: Microsoft Teams: live captions profanity filter now off by default
summary: Hold: the risk rationale says Microsoft Learn documents no admin policy for the captions filter, although the briefing itself accurately reports a Teams Rooms release note saying administrators can disable that filtering. The roadmap facts and the live-caption policy path and command check out, but the translated-caption licensing statement needs qualifications and several assertions about unchanged behaviour have no supporting passage.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Default state on means this default change reaches affected users without administrator action.
claims.quote: This change will only affect users who have never configured their live captions profanity filter preference. ... some users may begin seeing unfiltered profanity in live captions by default after this rollout.

claims.claim: The Live captions setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Live captions.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. ... From the drop-down for Live captions, select Not enabled, but users can enable(default value) or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled turns off live captions for users with that policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off live captions for users with this policy, run the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: Live captions is a per-user meeting policy setting.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy and applies during a meeting.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no admin policy for the captions profanity filter as of November 2026.
claims.quote: IT admins can turn on captions by default for all calls and meetings, as well as turn off the filtering of any profanity in captions and transcripts as necessary.
claims.fix: Replace the risk rationale with 'Medium. Users who never set a preference may see unfiltered profanity in live captions. Microsoft release notes disagree about administrator control of caption filtering, and the linked caption-policy pages do not give a profanity-filter setting.' This preserves the conflict already reported in Governance controls.

claims.quote: turn off the filtering of any profanity in captions and transcripts as necessary. To configure calling and meeting policies in the Teams admin center, see Enable call captions and Manage live captions.

## November 04, 2026
